sections.heading: What Does a Product Strategy Consultant Do?
intro: A [product strategy](/product-strategy) consultant helps a business decide which customer problems and product opportunities deserve investment, and how those decisions connect to commercial goals.

The work is not simply producing a roadmap. It means diagnosing where the product and market have drifted apart, gathering evidence, making trade-offs explicit and turning the resulting strategy into decisions the delivery team can act on.

sections.heading: Product Strategy Consulting From Customer Evidence to Roadmap
sections.intro: Start with the problem, not the backlog.

steps.title: Customer problem
steps.body: Define whose problem matters and what evidence exists that it is worth solving.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.body: Bring together customer research, product behaviour, market context and commercial signals.

steps.title: Strategic bets
steps.body: Decide where the product can create meaningful customer and business value.

steps.title: Prioritisation
steps.body: Make the trade-offs visible rather than allowing every request onto the roadmap.

steps.title: Delivery
steps.body: Translate decisions into journeys, prototypes, requirements and work the team can execute.

steps.title: Outcome
steps.body: Measure what happened and feed the evidence back into the next decision.

sections.targetKeyword: when to hire product strategy consultant
sections.heading: When to Hire a Product Strategy Consultant

items.title: The roadmap has become a request list
items.body: Customers, Sales and internal teams all have reasonable requests, but there is no shared logic for what wins.

items.title: Growth has changed the product problem
items.body: The product found a market, but the next stage needs clearer choices about segment, proposition or where to invest.

items.title: A major decision needs evidence
items.body: A fundraise, acquisition, new market or significant product investment creates a decision that deserves more than internal opinion.

items.title: Delivery is busy but direction is unclear
items.body: The team ships, but it is difficult to explain which customer or commercial outcome the work is intended to change.

sections.heading: Product Strategy Consultant Deliverables That Teams Can Use

items.title: Problem and evidence view
items.body: A clear account of the customer problem, available evidence and the assumptions that still need testing.

items.title: Strategic choices
items.body: Explicit product bets and trade-offs connected to customer and commercial outcomes.

items.title: Prioritisation
items.body: A decision model for what moves forward, what waits and why.

items.title: Roadmap direction
items.body: A roadmap organised around outcomes and initiatives rather than an undifferentiated feature list.

items.title: Delivery artefacts
items.body: Where useful, prototypes, user journeys, requirements and stories that keep the strategic intent connected to execution.

items.q: How is product strategy consulting different from product management?
items.a: Product strategy consulting focuses on the choices that determine where the product should compete, which customer problems deserve investment and how product decisions support the business. Product management also includes the ongoing work of coordinating [discovery](/product-strategy/discovery), prioritisation and delivery. Commview can work at strategy level and stay hands-on through execution.

items.q: What does a product strategy consultant actually deliver?
items.a: A product strategy consultant can deliver customer and market evidence, a clear problem definition, strategic bets, prioritisation logic, roadmap direction and the decision principles behind them. The exact output depends on the problem. Commview can also turn decisions into prototypes, user journeys, requirements and delivery-ready work where that helps.

items.q: When should we hire a product strategy consultant?
items.a: Hire a product strategy consultant when an important product decision lacks enough clarity or evidence to make confidently. Common signals include roadmap paralysis, post-product-market-fit drift, a major strategic change or a backlog dominated by competing requests. The value comes from improving the decision before more delivery effort is committed.

sections.heading: The roadmap should be the consequence of the strategy, not the strategy itself.
sections.body: We can help turn customer and commercial evidence into product choices the team can actually execute.
